provenance.human-curated: A person checked it against the primary source. Ground truth: where it disagrees with any other vector, it wins.
provenance.hand-checked: Taken from a worked example in the research doc, the unpublished study the spec started from (the spec's introduction).
provenance.engine-output: Taken from an implementation's tests or output (the Gorsuch library's), or computed from a source's records (CAP's case metadata, with the court code registry/cap-courts.json gives) by the spec's rules; it shows what the data and an implementation give, not what is correct.
provenance.spec-derived: Constructed from the spec's rules to exercise an edge case; not yet checked by a person.

parse.jsonl.checks: A validator accepts key; a parser returns parts and decision; formatting parts gives key back.

fields.parts: {jurisdiction, court, docket, decided, decision_ordinal (1 when unmarked), role (null for a decision), authors (list), part_ordinal (null for a decision, 1 when unmarked), revised (null when absent), fallback (true for an rpt. docket)}

reject.jsonl.checks: A validator rejects key, and SHOULD report error.

fields.layer: syntax: the ABNF and the regex reject it; semantic: they accept it and the validity rules of section 2.3 reject it

compute.jsonl.checks: A producer given facts, the court registry (registry/courts.json), the CAP court table (registry/cap-courts.json), the reporter registry (registry/reporters.json) and the judges fixture emits key, or refuses with error.

fields.facts: {jurisdiction (informational: the key's jurisdiction is the registry's for the court and date, spec section 3), court, or cap_court in its place (a CAP court id, translated through registry/cap-courts.json for the decision date, spec section 4), docket (as printed, or null), decided (as far as established: an ISO 8601 date, or reduced precision, a year and month or a year, which the key zeroes, spec section 6.2; or null), printed_decided? (the date as the printing prints it, for the printed-date alias, spec section 6.3; decided when absent), second_sources? (other sources' dates for the decision, [{date, kind}], kind official, human-curated, courtlistener, engine-output, printing, ...; spec section 13.3), printed_ordinal? (the decision's position in printed order for the printed-date alias; 1 when absent), decision_ordinal?, role?, authors?, part_ordinal?, revised?, reporter_citation? (the official citation, {volume, reporter, page}, or, from 0.6.0, the citation as the source prints it, `1 Mass. 1`, `2011-NMCA-108`; a volume numbered with a fraction is written as printed, 81 1/2; a citation that isn't a volume, a reporter and a page of decimal digits is not a reporter citation, spec section 5.6), parallel_citations? (from 0.6.0, #50: the decision's other citations as the source prints them, which decide the fallback citation of a Supreme Court decision a source files under another court, spec section 4), printed_in? (from 0.5.0, P1b: the volume and page the source's volume prints the decision on, and that volume's reporter, {volume, reporter, page}), volume_decisions? (from 0.5.0, P1a: the decisions in the volume the decision was taken from, in printed order, this one included, each {decided, printed_decided?, reporter_citation?, printed_in?}; a producer may list only those that share the decision's date), volume_position? (this decision's 1-based position in volume_decisions), page_decisions? (every decision that begins on the reporter page, in printed order, this one included: {docket (as printed, or null), decided, printed_decided?}), page_position? (this decision's 1-based position in page_decisions)}. Under the reporter fallback, volume_decisions and volume_position, or (0.4.0's inputs) page_decisions and page_position, give the decision ordinal (spec section 5.6)
fields.key: expected key, when the producer succeeds
fields.fallback: true when key uses the rpt. fallback
fields.error: refusal class, spec section 12, when it refuses
fields.aliases: key-shaped aliases (key references) for the other dockets of a consolidated case, when the vector checks them (spec sections 5.1, 11.1)
fields.printed_alias: the expected printed-date alias, when the vector checks it (spec section 6.3)
fields.provisional: whether the key is minted provisional, when the vector checks it (spec section 13.3)

decisions.jsonl.checks: A producer holding printings, the links it has between them, a person's rulings on them and the reporter registry (registry/reporters.json, or the vector's fixture in its place) gives the decisions they are, each with its key or refusal, as minted into an empty ledger (spec sections 5.9, 7.1, 13.2; from 0.6.0, rulings from 0.6.2).

fields.printings: [{id (the printing's identifier, a cap: alias where it is CAP's), candidate (the decision key sections 3 to 12 compute from that printing alone), reporter (its volume's reporter slug), volume (the volume as the source numbers it), page and position (where the decision begins in the volume: page, then position on the page), name (the case name the printing prints), citations (the citations the source lists for the printing, its own and its parallel citations, as printed)}]
fields.links: the producer's links between printings, [{printings: [id, id], source}], source courtlistener (a CourtListener cluster), official (the court's record or docket, or the official reporter's tables) or human-curated (a person's ruling); a citation two printings both list is a link too, and needs no entry (spec section 5.9)
fields.reporters: a fixture standing in for parts of the reporter registry (official, editions), when the vector needs entries the registry doesn't have
fields.rulings: a person's rulings on the printings (spec sections 5.9 and 7.1, from 0.6.2, D167), standing in for the rulings a producer holds; absent means none: [{id (the ruling's identifier, which conflicts name), printings (the ids it rules on, two or more), ruling (one-decision or distinct-decisions), key_printing (one-decision only, optional: the printing whose docket segment or fallback citation the key takes where the official-reporter table can't decide, section 5.9), evidence (what the person checked), by (who ruled), date (when, YYYY-MM-DD)}]. A one-decision ruling links its printings as a human-curated link does
fields.decisions: the expected decisions in minting order: [{printings (ids, sorted), key}] or [{printings, error}], error printings-disagree or shared-candidate (spec section 12); conflicts (from 0.6.2): the ids of the rulings the decision contradicts, which the producer reports (sections 5.9, 7.1), absent when there are none

docket.jsonl.checks: The court's docket profile (from registry/courts.json) maps printed to segment, or refuses with error.

fields.decided: decision date, when the court's profile depends on it (absent: the court's last profile)

byline.jsonl.checks: A producer maps the name a byline prints to a judge slug through the judges fixture's names and printed forms, for the court, or refuses (spec section 10.2).

fields.printed: the judge's name as the byline prints it, misprints included
fields.author: expected judge slug

alias.jsonl.checks: printed normalizes to alias under scheme; alias matches the alias grammar; resolves_to lists the keys a resolver returns.

fields.scheme: alias scheme, spec section 11.1 (crk for a key-shaped alias, written as a key reference, section 2.6; crk-printed for a printed-date alias, section 6.3)
fields.printed: identifier as printed, when the vector tests normalization

ledger.jsonl.checks: A publisher's minted-key ledger confirms or advances a candidate key (mint vectors), or a resolver follows replaced-by from a key to the decision's current key (resolve vectors) (spec sections 13.1 to 13.4).

fields.ledger: the ledger before the step: [{key (a decision key), decision (the publisher's identifier for the decision), status (active, replaced or errata), replaced_by? (a key), provisional? (true when marked, spec section 13.3)}]
fields.decision: mint vectors: the decision being keyed; resolve vectors: the expected decision
fields.candidate: mint vectors: the key sections 3 to 12 compute
fields.resolve: resolve vectors: the key given to the resolver
fields.key: mint vectors: the key the ledger gives the decision; resolve vectors: the current key
fields.minted: mint vectors: false when the ledger confirms the decision's active key and nothing is minted
fields.replaces: mint vectors: the decision's active key that the new key supersedes, or null
fields.provisional: resolve vectors: whether the current key is marked provisional

errata.jsonl.checks: errata is a valid errata list (schema/crk-errata.schema.json, spec section 13.4) whose seq numbers 1, 2, ... with no gaps, whose keys are valid keys (section 2.3), and which, given previous, holds every entry of previous unchanged and in order; or it is not, for the stated problem.

fields.previous: the version published before it, when the vector checks the append-only rule
fields.valid: true when errata meets every rule
fields.problem: when invalid: schema, seq, key or append-only
